text: Broker Joshua Leonard sends 80.6 percent of his referrals to Howard Institute, supplies 50.9 percent of that clinic's claims, holds a 17.3 percent stake in it, and has received 7,988 dollars in transfers from the clinic against roughly 5,008 dollars of expected declared commission — a 7.1 percent excess over the pair's billing. Each leg has an honest reading (exclusive partnerships exist; declared stakes exist; commissions vary), but mutual concentration plus equity plus money beyond the declared relationship is the closed-loop kickback shape, and the clinic's lack of accreditation removes the usual in-house-facilitation explanation. The stake is the strongest single fact: referral steering pays twice when you own the destination. Next step: reconcile the clinic-to-broker transfers against any written commission agreement; the unexplained margin is the case.
